newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Grand Orient in HK$358 mln rights issue.
newsitem.headline: Grand Orient in HK$358 mln rights issue.

text.p: Hong Kong's Grand Orient Holdings Ltd said in a statement on Monday it plans to raise about HK$358 million before expenses through a rights issue of 275.49 million new shares.

The company said it would issue one rights share for every existing share held on February 27, 1997 at HK$1.30 per rights share. The rights price represents a discount of about 33.3 percent to Friday's closing price of HK$1.95 per share.

Grand Orient said it intended to use about HK$220 million of the proceeds to upgrade and enlarge its property portfolio in Hong Kong and China, about HK$100 million to repay bank debt and about HK$29 million for working capital.

"It is the current intention of the directors to dispose of those properties in Hong Kong which generate low rental yield, under the presently favourable property market conditions, and to expand the group's property portfolio by acquiring quality properties in Hong Kong and the People's Republic of China," the statement said said.
"It is the intention of the directors to strengthen the group's activity in financial services which is expected to make substantial contributions to the group's future earnings," it added.
Grand Orient said it had expanded its financial services business in 1996 and as on December 31, 1996 had a loan portfolio of about HK$100 million.

The company said its major shareholders Oseda Investments Ltd and Kingmass Worldwide Ltd hold 22.24 percent and 6.07 percent respectively of the company's existing share capital and have undertaken to accept their full allotment of rights shares amounting to a total 77.99 million rights shares, or about 28.31 percent of the issue.

Grand Orient executive chairman Teoh Guan Hock holds a stake in Oseda and managing director Chung Toi Chiu has a stake in Kingmass Worldwide. The balance of the rights shares will be underwritten by Shenyin Wanguo Capital (H.K.) Ltd.
